label: Look-alike stops in a blind zone
blurb: What happens. Two look-alike vehicles pass CAM-W. One of them pulls off inside blind zone G2 and never reaches CAM-N. Watch the blue bands, then the alert when a window closes empty. The monitor proves one is missing without guessing which; the conventional tracker names the wrong one.

label: Swap on the side track
blurb: What happens. One vehicle leaves on the NW side track inside G2 and a different vehicle joins the road there. The count at CAM-N still matches. Watch the monitor flag both the missing departure and the arrival that no departure explains.

label: Dust blinds CAM-N
blurb: What happens. Every vehicle arrives, but dust covers CAM-N while they pass. Watch the monitor refuse to give an all-clear and report a coverage gap, while the conventional tracker raises a false alarm and a count-only check says all clear.

label: Vehicle leaves on the side track
blurb: What happens. One vehicle turns onto the NW side track inside G2 and leaves the map. Watch the search area cover the blind road segment and the side track, and the drone tasked toward it.

label: Normal convoy
blurb: What happens. A convoy drives the whole loop and every vehicle arrives at every camera. Watch the tip-offs go out and every link settle to all accounted for, with no alerts.

label: Limit: look-alike swap
blurb: Known limit. A vehicle leaves on the side track and a look-alike joins in its place. Appearance and timing both fit, so no camera-only method can tell, and this monitor also reports all clear. A plate read or a PTZ zoom on arrivals, both in the plan, is what closes this gap.
